create_entry.default: The sensor stays unknown until you teach it both states. Go to **Settings** > **Devices & services** > **Helpers**, select the sensor, select the settings icon, then **Local vision options**. Teach one frame of each state, for example door open and door closed. If a state is not visible right now, teach it later.

error.blank_frame: The camera shows nothing, for example because it is offline or covered. Check the camera and try again.
error.blank_region: There is nothing to compare in this region, for example because it shows a plain surface. Make the region larger or move it to a part with some detail.
error.invalid_frame: The camera returned an image that Home Assistant can't read. Check the camera's settings and try again.
error.invalid_horizontal_range: The left edge must be smaller than the right edge.
error.invalid_vertical_range: The top edge must be smaller than the bottom edge.
error.no_suggestion: No meter was found in the frame. Enter the regions yourself.
error.too_many_decimal_wheels: There can't be more wheels after the decimal point than wheels.

data_description.counterclockwise: Turn this on if the numbers on the dial run counterclockwise.

dial.description:
![Current frame with the regions outlined]({preview})

Put the region around dial {number}, centered on its axis. Dial 1 counts the largest steps, for example ×0.1, the next one ten times smaller.
dial.title: Pointer dial {number} of {count}

data_description.decimal_wheels: The rightmost wheels that count fractions, often red or behind a separator. 0 if all wheels count whole units.
data_description.dial_count: Pointer dials that count below the last wheel, for example ×0.1 and ×0.01. 0 if the meter has none.
data_description.rotation: Degrees counterclockwise that turn the frame so the digits are level. The preview shows the turned frame, and the regions are edges in it. 0 if the digits are level already.
data_description.wheels: All wheels in the region, also those after the decimal point.

digits.description:
![Current frame with the regions outlined]({preview})

Put the region tightly around all counter wheels, from the first to the last digit, without the frame around them. 0 is the left or top edge of the frame, 100 the right or bottom edge. If the digits are not level, set the rotation first; the next preview shows the turned frame.
digits.title: Counter wheels

data_description.device_class: What the meter counts. This sets the units and where the sensor fits in the Energy dashboard.
data_description.entity_id: The camera that shows the meter.
data_description.name: For example, Water meter. The sensor is added to the camera's device, so the device name is shown in front.

meter.description: Create a sensor that reads a meter with counter wheels and, if it has them, pointer dials. Everything runs locally. The camera should look straight at the meter and the digits should be sharp and lit, also at night.
meter.title: Meter reading

menu_option_descriptions.digits: Go back and adjust the regions.
menu_option_descriptions.meter_finish: Create the sensor with these regions.

meter_confirm.title: Check the regions

meter_regions.description:
![Current frame]({preview})

Next, mark the window with the counter wheels and each pointer dial. You can enter the regions yourself, or let Home Assistant suggest them and adjust them afterwards.

menu_option_descriptions.digits: Enter the edges of each region in percent of the frame.
menu_option_descriptions.suggest: Look for the meter in the current frame and fill in the regions and the rotation. This is an early version that can miss the meter or mark something else, such as a serial number, so check every region afterwards.

meter_regions.title: Meter regions

data_description.max_rate: A reading that rises faster than this is rejected as a misread. Leave it empty for a value well above a household's use, such as 10 m³ for water or gas and 100 kWh for electricity. A higher value lets more misreads through.
data_description.unit: The unit the counter wheels count in.

meter_unit.description: Choose the unit printed on the meter.
meter_unit.title: Unit

data_description.bottom: Where the region ends, in percent of the frame height from the top edge.
data_description.left: Where the region starts, in percent of the frame width from the left edge.
data_description.right: Where the region ends, in percent of the frame width from the left edge.
data_description.top: Where the region starts, in percent of the frame height from the top edge.

region.description:
![Current frame with the region outlined]({preview})

Choose the part of the frame the sensor watches. 0 is the left or top edge of the frame, 100 the right or bottom edge. The next step shows the result.

Put the region around what changes, such as the door itself. Leave out things that move for other reasons, such as people, plants, or things that get moved around.

You can't change the region later without adding the sensor again.
region.title: Choose the region

region_confirm.description:
![Current frame with the region outlined]({preview})

The sensor only looks at the outlined region.

menu_option_descriptions.finish: Create the sensor with this region.
menu_option_descriptions.region: Go back and adjust the edges.

region_confirm.title: Check the region

data_description.device_class: What the region shows. This sets the state names, such as Open and Closed or Detected and Clear, and the icon.
data_description.entity_id: The camera that shows what you want to watch.
data_description.name: For example, Garage door. The sensor is added to the camera's device, so the device name is shown in front, for example Garage camera Garage door. Don't repeat the camera name here.

state.description: Create a binary sensor that recognizes the state of a part of the camera view, such as a garage door that is open or closed. You teach it with example frames from the camera. Everything runs locally.
state.title: State of an area

user.description: Everything runs locally, no image leaves Home Assistant.

menu_option_descriptions.meter: A sensor with the reading of a water, gas or electricity meter with counter wheels, for the Energy dashboard.
menu_option_descriptions.state: A binary sensor for a part of the camera view, such as a garage door that is open or closed. You teach it with example frames.

user.title: What should be recognized?

camera_unavailable.message: Could not get a frame from {entity_id}: {error}

invalid_frame.message: The camera returned an image that could not be decoded: {error}

abort.correct_successful: The value was set. The next readings are checked against it.
abort.not_loaded: The sensor is not loaded right now. Check it under **Settings** > **Devices & services** > **Helpers**, then open the options again.
abort.teach_successful: The frame was taught. To teach another one, open the options again. Teach more frames when the region looks different, for example at night or in the other state.

error.blank_frame: The camera shows nothing, for example because it is dark or offline. A new frame is shown above. Try again.
error.blank_region: The region in this frame has nothing to compare, for example because it is dark or shows a plain surface. A new frame is shown above. Try again when the region shows more detail.
error.nothing_selected: Select at least one frame to remove.

data_description.value: The reading on the meter, in the unit of the sensor.

correct.description: Enter the value shown on the meter, for example after a wrong reading or a new meter. The value can also be lower than the current one, statistics then count from it as from a new meter.
correct.title: Correct the value

menu_option_descriptions.remove: Remove frames taught with the wrong state or that no longer match the view.
menu_option_descriptions.teach: Take the current camera frame and tell the sensor what it shows.

data_description.frames: Each entry shows the state the frame was taught as and when it was taught.

remove.description: Remove frames that were taught with the wrong state or that no longer match the view, for example after the camera was moved. If a state has no frames left, the sensor is unknown until you teach that state again.
remove.title: Remove taught frames

data_description.state: Only teach a frame that clearly shows one state.

teach.description:
![Current frame with the region outlined]({preview})

Teach at least one frame of each state. More frames in different light, such as day, night, or with the lights on, make the sensor more reliable.

Frames taught so far: {counts}. The sensor shows unknown while it is unsure.
teach.title: Teach the current frame
